transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because... I've been having a little bit of a hard time lately. I know it probably sounds really silly, and I hate to even bring it up because I don't want to come across as vain or anything, but... I just can't seem to stop focusing on the left side of my face. 

It just looks really uneven and kind of puffy to me. I notice it constantly on my video calls for work—I do computer support, so I'm on camera a lot—and in the photos from my salsa dancing group. Everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything at all, which is sweet of them, but... it's just really starting to get in the way of my job and my social life. 

I hope it's okay that I came in to talk about something like this? Does that make sense?
Does your perception of your face being uneven and puffy stay the same all the time, or does it change?

Um, gosh, that's a really good question. I'm actually not entirely sure? 

I guess... I mean, I just notice it so much, but I haven't really paid attention to whether it fluctuates or stays exactly the same. I'm sorry, I feel like I should know that! I just know it always bothers me when I see myself on camera or in the mirror, but I couldn't say for sure if it gets worse or better at certain times. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I know it's not very specific. I can try to start keeping track of it if that would be more helpful for you to know?
Has your concern about the left side of your face been causing you a lot of distress?

Um, well... I guess "distress" sounds like such a strong word. I definitely don't want to sound dramatic or anything! I know there are people dealing with much bigger problems in the world, so I feel a little silly even complaining about it. 

It's more just... really frustrating, I guess? Like, it bothers me enough that it's on my mind a lot, especially right before I have to log on for work or go out, and it does get me down sometimes. But I try really hard to just push through it and not let it show or ruin my day. 

I hope I'm not overreacting by coming in for this? I just want to make sure I'm handling it the right way... is it okay that it bothers me this much?
Has your concern about the left side of your face been interfering with your daily activities?

Um... well... I mean, I try really hard not to let it interfere, you know? I want to be a good employee and a good friend. But... I guess it has gotten a little bit in the way recently. I feel terrible even admitting this... 

There have been a few times where I was just so caught up trying to fix how I looked that I ended up missing some ticket deadlines for work. And... I've joined a few video calls late. It's so unprofessional, I know. My supervisor actually brought it up during my last performance review, which was just so embarrassing. I promised her I'd do better. 

And... socially, I guess I've been pulling back a tiny bit? Like, I've skipped a couple of my salsa nights, and some community events, just because I knew there would be a lot of photos taken and I just couldn't face it. 

I know I shouldn't let it affect my life like this, and I'm really trying to fix it. Do you think it's normal to struggle with this kind of thing sometimes? I just want to make sure I'm not being completely unreasonable.
Is it specifically the unevenness and puffiness of the left side of your face that bothers you, or is it more about how you look in general?

Um, well... I guess it's mostly just the left side of my face. I mean, I try to take care of myself in general, you know? I want to look presentable and professional. But... it's really just this one specific thing that I can't seem to stop focusing on. 

It's the unevenness and the puffiness on that left side. It just... it looks so obvious to me, especially when I'm on those work video calls, or when someone tags me in a photo from salsa class. I just fixate on it. And the funny thing is, I've brought it up to my friends and my mom, and they all swear they don't see what I'm talking about. They say I look completely normal. Which makes me feel a little crazy, to be honest. 

I really don't want to be someone who is obsessed with their appearance, because I know that sounds so shallow. But it's just... it's really starting to mess with my work and my social life, like I mentioned before. I just can't seem to let it go, even when people tell me it's fine. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just want to be honest with you about what's actually bothering me, even if it sounds a little silly.
Do you think it's possible that the unevenness and puffiness on the left side of your face might not be as noticeable to others as it is to you?

Um... yes, I mean, logically, I really want to agree with you. I know you're probably exactly right. Like I mentioned, my mom and my friends keep telling me they don't see anything at all, and I really do try to believe them! I don't want to be difficult or argue with anyone about it. 

But... I guess that's honestly why I finally came in to see you. Because even though everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything, I just... I can't stop focusing on it. It's like my brain won't let me ignore it. Every time I have to look at myself on those work video calls, or when I see those salsa photos, all I can see is how uneven and puffy that left side looks. 

I know I shouldn't be so fixated on it, and I feel so embarrassed admitting this, but it's just constantly on my mind. And it's starting to really mess with my work and my social life, which I hate. I want to be able to just brush it off like a normal person would. 

Do you think... I mean, is it okay that I'm having such a hard time believing them, even if they are right? I just want to make sure I'm not completely losing touch with reality.
Do you think there's any possibility that the left side of your face actually looks normal, and you're just perceiving it as uneven and puffy?

Um... well... yes, I mean, I really want to believe that's possible. I know I keep repeating myself, and I'm so sorry if I'm being frustrating! It's just... I really do try to tell myself that it's normal, especially since my mom and my friends swear they don't see anything. I want to be reasonable, I really do.

But... I guess that's exactly why I'm here. Because even when I try to tell myself it might actually look normal, I just... I literally can't stop focusing on it. It's like I'm completely preoccupied with it. Whenever I log onto a video call for work, or if I see a picture from my salsa class, my eyes just dart right to that left side, and all I see is the puffiness and the unevenness. 

It feels so silly to even be talking about it this much, but it really is starting to mess with my work deadlines and making me miss social things, like I was saying before. I just... I can't seem to shake this intense focus on it, no matter how hard I try to convince myself it's fine. 

Does that make me sound completely irrational? I just want to be a good patient and give you the right information, but it's so hard to explain why I can't just let it go.
If someone you trust were to reassure you that your face looks perfectly fine, would that make you feel better about your appearance?

Um... well, honestly... they actually do reassure me. All the time. My mom, my friends... they're always telling me I look perfectly fine and that I have nothing to worry about. And I always tell them thank you, and I really try to just smile and agree with them, because I don't want to seem ungrateful or... or vain, you know? 

But... inside... it doesn't really help. I mean, maybe for a split second I feel a little relief, but then I just go right back to... to checking the mirror or worrying about the next video call. It's like their words just don't stick in my brain, no matter how much I want them to. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm just ignoring their support, and I promise I'm not trying to be difficult. I really do want their reassurance to work. Is it... is it bad that it doesn't? I hope I'm not coming across as too stubborn.
Is there anything else besides your appearance that you worry about or feel is not perfect?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to do a good job at work and everything, but... no, it's really just my face. I don't obsess over, like, keeping my apartment perfectly clean or anything like that. I mean, I like things tidy, but I'm pretty normal about it, I think. 

It's just... this one specific thing with my appearance that I can't seem to get past. I hope that's okay? I mean, I know it's probably weird to be so hyper-focused on just one thing, but I promise I'm not, like, a perfectionist about everything else in my life. Is that... does that make sense for someone in my situation?

Does your concern about the left side of your face bother you more in certain situations, like when you're on video calls or taking photos, or is it something that bothers you all the time, even when you're alone?

Um... well, to answer your question—and I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record, I'm so sorry!—it definitely gets a lot worse in those specific situations. Like I was saying earlier, the whole reason I finally decided to come in is because I just can't stop focusing on how uneven and puffy the left side looks whenever I'm on those work video calls or seeing pictures from my salsa class. It's just... it's really starting to mess with my work and my social life, even though everyone keeps telling me they don't see what I'm seeing. 

But... as for when I'm alone... um, I really want to say I'm totally fine when I'm by myself, but honestly, it still bothers me then, too. It's kind of always running in the background. Even if no one is looking at me, I'm thinking about it, or stressing about the next time I have to be on camera. I try so hard to just relax and not think about it when I'm alone in my apartment, because I know it's not productive to just sit there and worry. 

Is that... does that answer what you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details, I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough.
Do you think that someone who didn't know you and saw you for the first time would notice the unevenness and puffiness on the left side of your face?

Um... well... I guess I'd like to think they wouldn't notice? I mean, I try really hard to position myself or do my hair in a way that hides it, so maybe a stranger wouldn't see it right away. I don't want people to think I look awful the second they meet me. 

But... honestly, in my head, I feel like it's the very first thing anyone sees. Like I said, the whole reason I'm here is because I just can't stop fixating on how uneven and puffy that left side looks, especially on those work calls or in the pictures from salsa class. I know my friends and family say they don't see it, but... I just feel like a stranger might, you know? Because they don't love me and they aren't trying to spare my feelings. 

I'm really trying not to let it ruin things, but it's just... it's really starting to mess with my work and my social life, because I'm so worried about what people are seeing. I hope that doesn't make me sound too crazy or self-obsessed. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer.
Do you think it's possible that the unevenness and puffiness you see on the left side of your face is not something that anyone else can see, even if you show it to them?

Um... yeah, I guess... logically, that has to be possible, right? I mean, I really don't want to sound stubborn or like I'm arguing with you or my friends. I know I keep repeating myself—and I'm so sorry for bringing it back to this again—but that's really the whole reason I came in. I just can't stop focusing on how uneven and puffy the left side of my face looks on my video calls and in those salsa photos. And... well, everyone does keep telling me they don't see anything, even when I point right to the exact spot. 

So, I try to believe them, I really do, because I don't want to be difficult. But it's just so hard to ignore when it looks so obvious to me, and it's starting to really mess with my work and my social life. I really want to be able to just accept that maybe it is just something I'm seeing, if that's what you think is happening? I hope it's okay that I'm struggling to let it go. Am I answering your question the right way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Do you think it's possible that the left side of your face looks perfectly normal, but you're just misinterpreting what you see?

Um... yeah, I suppose... I mean, I really want to believe that's possible. I don't want to be someone who just makes things up in her head, you know? I want to be reasonable. 

It's just... I'm so sorry, I know I'm probably frustrating you by saying this again, but it's just so hard for me to wrap my head around it. Like, I came in because I just can't stop focusing on how uneven and puffy that left side looks, especially on those video calls and in my salsa photos. And I know I keep saying that, and I know everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything... but it's just so vivid to me. 

I'm really trying to be open to the idea that I'm misinterpreting it, especially since it's starting to mess with my work and my social life so much. I really don't want to be difficult or dismiss what you're saying. If you think it's possible that it looks perfectly normal and I'm just seeing it wrong, I'll definitely try to look at it from that perspective. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too resistant... I really do want to figure this out and get better.
If you were completely convinced that the left side of your face looks normal, would your concern about it go away?

Um... yes, I think so? I mean, if I could somehow just... fully believe that it looks normal, then I wouldn't need to worry about it, right? I'd love for that to happen. I really would. 

It's just... I'm so sorry, I feel like a broken record, and I don't want to annoy you. But the whole reason I'm here is because I just can't stop focusing on how uneven and puffy the left side of my face looks on my video calls and in those salsa photos. Even though everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything, it's just... it's stuck in my head, and it's starting to mess with my work and my social life. 

But yes, if I could be completely convinced it was normal, I think the concern would go away. I really want to get to that point. I hope I'm answering this the right way... I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me. Is that what you were asking?
Does your concern about the left side of your face ever completely go away, even if it's just for a short period of time?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I wish I could say yes, because I know I should be able to just put it out of my mind, right? I really try to. But... no, it doesn't ever completely go away. 

Even when I'm trying really hard to focus on something else, or if I'm having a good day... it's always kind of there in the back of my mind. Like, I'll be talking to a client at work, and suddenly I'll wonder if they can see how puffy it is, or I'll be out with friends and just feel this urge to check a mirror or angle my face away. I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit obsessive, and I really don't want to be that kind of person. I'm trying my best to manage it. 

I just... I haven't found a way to make the thought stop completely yet. Is it bad that it's always on my mind like that? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I just want to be honest with you so you know what's going on. Does that make sense?
Do you think your perception of your face being uneven and puffy is based on reality?

Um... well... I guess that's the hard part, right? I mean, when I look in the mirror or see those photos, it looks *so* real to me. It feels like a fact. But... I know everyone else says they don't see it, and I really respect your professional opinion. 

So, I don't know... maybe it isn't based on reality? Or at least, maybe not as much as I think it is? I'm trying really hard to accept that it might just be my mind playing tricks on me, because I don't want to be stubborn or ignore what everyone is telling me. I really want to be cooperative. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very clear answer. I just... I struggle to tell what's real and what's just my anxiety about it, you know? Does that sound like I'm making progress, being open to that? I hope I'm looking at this the right way...
Do you think it's possible that your perception of your face is not based on how it actually looks?

Um... yes, I think it's definitely possible. I mean, I really hope it's possible. 

Since everyone—my friends, my family, and you—keeps telling me that they don't see the puffiness or the unevenness, I'm really trying to trust that. I know I shouldn't just rely on my own eyes when everyone else is saying something different, right? I want to be reasonable about this. 

So, yes, I'm very open to the idea that maybe my brain is just... filtering things wrong, or making it seem worse than it actually is. I don't want to be someone who just refuses to listen to reason. I'm really trying to take everyone's perspective into account, not just my own. Is that the kind of mindset I should be having? I just want to make sure I'm approaching this the right way to get better.
Do you think your perception of your face being uneven and puffy might be a product of your own thoughts rather than an actual physical characteristic?

Um... yeah, I suppose it really could be. I mean, you're the doctor, and I completely trust your perspective on this. I really want to agree with you.

I guess... the whole reason I finally came in to see you is because I just can't seem to stop focusing on it, even if it is just my own thoughts. Like, whenever I'm on video calls for work—I do computer support—or when I see photos of myself from my salsa dancing group... all I can focus on is how uneven and puffy that left side looks. 

I'm actually a little embarrassed to admit how much it bothers me, because everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything at all. I know I should just let it go. But it's starting to mess with my work and my social life a bit, and I really don't want to let it affect my performance or make me a bad friend. I try to hide it, but it's getting hard. 

So if you think it's just my thoughts creating this, I am more than willing to believe that and work on it. Does recognizing that mean I'm on the right track? I just really want to do whatever I need to do to fix this, if that makes sense.
Do you think you would still believe your face is uneven and puffy even if a plastic surgeon told you it was perfectly normal?

Oh... wow, um. That's a really good question. I mean, I would really like to think that if an actual plastic surgeon told me it was perfectly normal, I would just... believe them immediately. Because they're the experts, right? Just like you. I definitely want to trust the professionals. 

But... if I'm being completely honest with you—and I really want to be a good patient and be honest—I think... maybe there would still be this tiny little voice in the back of my head wondering if they just didn't look closely enough at the left side? Or maybe they were just trying to be nice and make me feel better? 

I haven't actually gone to see a surgeon, so I don't know for absolute sure how I'd react. But I really, really hope I would just listen to them and finally let it go. I know it probably sounds terrible to admit that I might second-guess a specialist... I'm sorry, is it bad that I'm not one hundred percent sure? I really am trying to be as logical as possible about all of this.
Do you think you would still see your face as uneven and puffy even if you looked at it in a mirror with me right now?

Oh, um... I'm actually not really sure. I haven't ever tried looking in a mirror with someone else right there beside me, pointing things out. 

I'd really like to think that if you were standing right next to me, and you were telling me that everything looks completely normal, I would be able to just... see what you see. I really, really want to be able to do that. I want to trust your eyes more than mine. 

But... I don't know for absolute sure if my brain would just instantly fix the image, if that makes sense? Like, maybe I would still see a little bit of the puffiness at first, even if I was trying my absolute hardest not to. I hope I wouldn't, though. I really don't want to be stubborn or difficult about this. Do you think doing something like that—looking together—is something that usually helps people see things correctly? I'm completely willing to try it if you think it's a good idea.
